title: How much time passes on the ship?
hook: Compare a moving clock with the stationary frame.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: The Lorentz factor at 0.6c is 1/sqrt(1−0.6²) = 1.25. The moving clock measures the proper time between its own two events: 10/1.25 = 8 seconds.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: The Lorentz factor at 0.6c is 1/sqrt(1−0.6²) = 1.25. The moving clock measures the proper time between its own two events: 10/1.25 = 8 seconds.

claims.text: The Lorentz factor at 0.6c is 1/sqrt(1−0.6²) = 1.25. The moving clock measures the proper time between its own two events: 10/1.25 = 8 seconds. Special relativity: inertial motion at constant speed; the observer uses synchronized clocks in their own frame.
claims.source: Delta t = gamma Delta tau, gamma = 1/sqrt(1-beta²). beta=0.6 gives gamma=1.25.

recall.question: At 0.6c, a moving clock records 4 seconds between two ticks. How much time separates those events in the observer's rest frame?
recall.why: Multiply the proper interval by gamma=1.25: 4 × 1.25 = 5 seconds.
